1410.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. Salok Varan te Vadhik (the saloks beyond the vaars): by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (A young bride,) tall, full-bosomed, grave and full of pride, (says to her friend): How shall I bow to my mother-in-law? I cannot bend, because of my breasts. (The friend replies:) O friend, the mansions that stood like mountains, plastered with lime, those too I have seen falling; O young woman, take no pride in your breasts. ॥1॥
1410.2: Listen, O young woman with eyes like a deer's, to a word deep and boundless: having first recognised the goods well, only then should one make the deal. One should raise the cry against the wicked, and acclaim for the friends; O young woman, reflect on that cry through which the friends are met. Body and mind should be given to the friends: such joy is the most excellent. One should not set one's love on what is plainly passing away. Nanak is a sacrifice to those who have understood it in this way. ॥2॥
1410.3: If you would be a swimmer of the waters, ask those who know the art of swimming across; they are the truly wise: (with them) I would pass through these waves (of the world-ocean). ॥3॥
1410.4: Downpours, gales and floods, and waves by the hundred thousand are surging; call out to the True Guru, and there is no fear of the boat sinking. ॥4॥
1410.5: O Nanak, what has the world become! No guide on the path, no friend, has remained. Love among brothers and kin has been done away with; for the world's sake (people) have thrown away their faith. ॥5॥
1410.6: (At a death, people) cry alas, alas, and wail aloud; they beat their cheeks and tear (the hair of) their heads. Those who take the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) and keep patience (in his will): Nanak is a sacrifice to them. ॥6॥
1410.7: O mind, one should not waver on the crooked (path): run on the straight path. Behind is a fearsome tiger, ahead a lake of fire; my soul is caught in dread, and I have no other way. O Nanak, through the Guru one is released, and finds company with the Beloved Lord. ॥7॥
1410.8: The tiger dies and the mind is subdued in one who has the True Guru's teaching; he recognises his own self, meets the Lord, and does not die again. His hand does not sink into the mud, (when the Lord) beholds (him) with a single glance of grace. O Nanak, the Gurmukhs (those who follow the Guru) are saved: the Guru is the lake, and the true embankment. ॥8॥
1411.1: Seek and find the water, (and) the fire dies out; (but) without the Guru, the treasure-house, there is no water. (Without it) one is born and dies and is made to wander, even if (people) perform a hundred thousand rites. Jam (the messenger of Death), the toll-collector, does not touch one who walks in the True Guru's will. O Nanak, (his is) the stainless, deathless state: the Guru unites (him) in union with the Lord. ॥9॥
1411.2: In a little pond of brackish earth the crow bathes, scrubbing and scrubbing; (yet) its mind and body are filthy with faults, and its beak is filled with stench. In the company of crows, those foul birds, the swan did not know the lake (for what it is). Such is love with a Saakat (one who has turned from God); understand this, O wise ones, in (the Lord's) love. Hail the assembly of the Sants (saints), and do (your) deeds through the Guru: O Nanak, this is the pure bathing: the Guru is the pilgrimage-place and the river. ॥10॥
1411.3: What shall I count as the fruit of being born, when there is no devotion to the Lord, no love? What is worn and eaten is wasted, when in the mind is the love of another; seeing and hearing are false, and false is the speech of the mouth. O Nanak, praise the Naam; all else is Haumai (ego), coming and going. ॥11॥
1411.4: (Such people) are few, not many; the world is all show and coarse talk. ॥12॥
1411.5: O Nanak, one whom (the blow of love) strikes dies at once; no strength to live remains. One who dies by the blow: that stroke is accepted. It strikes the one whom (the Lord) strikes; then (only) is the stroke accepted. The arrow of love does not come out, once that all-wise one has shot it. ॥13॥
1411.6: Who can wash the vessel that was made unbaked? Mixing the five elements, a false show has been put together. When it pleases him, (he) will set the vessel right; awakening the Supreme Light, he will play the instrument (within). ॥14॥
1411.7: Those who are pitch-blind in mind do not know their duty, even when told. With the mind blind and the lotus (of the heart) upturned, they look utterly hideous. Some know how to speak and understand what is said: those men are wise and comely. Some have no feel for music, nor for the Vedas, nor the delight of song; they do not know the sweet from the bitter. Some have no success, no understanding, no grasp of sense, and do not know the mystery of the letters. O Nanak, those men are truly donkeys who, without any virtue, take pride (in themselves). ॥15॥
1411.8: He is a Brahmin who knows Brahm (God), who makes prayer, austerity and self-restraint his deeds, who keeps to the dharma of gentleness and contentment, who breaks his bonds and becomes free: such a Brahmin alone is worthy of worship. ॥16॥
1411.9: He is a Khatri (of the warrior caste) who is a hero in (good) deeds, who makes his body (an instrument) of charity and giving, who knows the field and sows the gift (in it): such a Khatri is accepted in the Lord's court. If he practises greed, avarice and falsehood, he himself receives (the fruit of) what he has done. ॥17॥
1411.10: Do not heat the body as an oven is heated, nor burn the bones as firewood; what wrong have the head and the feet done (you)? Cherish the Beloved within. ॥18॥
1412.1: The Husband (Lord) dwells in every heart; there is no heart without the Husband. O Nanak, those are the happy soul-brides in whom, through the Guru, he becomes manifest. ॥19॥
1412.2: If you long to play the game of love, place your head on your palm and come into my lane. If one is to set foot on this path, one should give one's head, and not hesitate. ॥20॥
1412.3: Friendship with the kiraars (those ever counting their gains) rests on falsehood, and its footing is false; O Mula, it is not known where death will come. ॥21॥
Mula: in the Sikh tradition, a man of Sialkot who hid from Guru Nanak rather than go with him, and died that day of a snakebite.
1412.4: Those without (spiritual) wisdom worship ignorance; blind is their conduct, (theirs is) the love of another. ॥22॥
1412.5: Without the Guru (there is no) wisdom, without dharma (no) meditation; without truth there is no credit, and not even the capital is left. ॥23॥
1412.6: (The Lord) sends man (into the world), and he rises and goes; there is no joy in such a thing. ॥24॥
1412.7: Ram grieves; he gathers his armies, and within him is the strength of command; an army of monkeys serves him, with boundless zeal for battle in mind and body; the ten-headed (Ravan) carried off Sita, and Lachhman died through a curse. O Nanak, the Creator is the one who does all: he makes and unmakes, and beholds (it all). ॥25॥

Ram and Ravan: in the Ramayana, Ram, the prince of Ayodhya, held to be an incarnation of Vishnu, and Ravan, the demon king of Lanka, whom Ram slew. Sita is Ram's wife, whom Ravan carried off, and Lachhman his brother; Hanuman is the servant of Ram.
1412.8: Ramchand grieves in his mind for Sita and for Lachhman; he called to mind Hanvantar (Hanuman), who had come (to him) through (destined) union. The deluded demon (Ravan) does not understand that God has done (all) these things. O Nanak, he is free of all need; what was written by past deeds is not erased (even) by Ram. ॥26॥
1412.9: The city of Lahore is poison, a havoc lasting a pahar and a quarter. ॥27॥
A pahar is about three hours.
1412.10: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The city of Lahore is a pool of Amrit (the nectar of the Name), the home of (the Lord's) praises. ॥28॥
Lahore is the birthplace of Guru Ram Das Ji.
1412.11: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). What is the sign of prosperity? There is no shortage of grain; prosperity has settled in the very house, (filled with) the clamour of girls and women; the seven women in the house mourn and wail; they weep over false concerns; what he takes he does not give (back); he earns his coins, (yet lives) in dread. ॥29॥
1412.12: O pool, you were all green, your lotuses the colour of gold; by what fault were you scorched, and your fair body turned black? (It replies:) O Nanak, my body has suffered loss; I know it: I do not find the water with which I had my companionship, at whose sight the body blossoms and takes on a fourfold colour. ॥30॥
1412.13: No one has lived to his fill, and no one has left with (his tasks) completed. The one with (divine) wisdom lives for ever and ever; honour comes only to the one whose awareness (is fixed on God). In saving and sparing, ever and ever, (life) has passed away like this. O Nanak, to whom should one complain? (Death) takes (one) away without even asking. ॥31॥
1412.14: Do not blame the Rai (the rich man): when he grows old, his understanding goes. He talks a great deal, so the blind one must fall into pits and ditches. ॥32॥
1412.15: All that the Perfect One has done is perfect; there is nothing too little or too much (in it). O Nanak, the Gurmukh knows it so; (such ones) merge in the Perfect One. ॥33॥
1413.1: Saloks, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Those are not to be called abhiagats (holy wanderers) in whose minds is restless wandering; O Nanak, what is given to them earns merit just like them. ॥1॥
1413.2: One who becomes a beggar for the supreme state of the fearless, stainless (Lord): O Nanak, rare is the one who is blessed to provide the food of such a one. ॥2॥
1413.3: Were I to become a pandit or an astrologer, or recite the four Vedas by heart, (still) in the nine regions (of the earth) I would be known by my own conduct and thought. ॥3॥
1413.4: Killing a Brahmin or a cow, (killing) a daughter, (taking) the grain of an evil-doer, curses upon curses, the leprosy of evil deeds, pride forever and ever: all these are earned, O Nanak, by those who forget the one Naam; all (other) cleverness is burnt away, and only the essence, (divine) wisdom, remains. ॥4॥
1413.5: What is written on the forehead from the beginning, no one can erase. O Nanak, what is written comes to pass; he alone understands (this) on whom is (the Lord's) glance of grace. ॥5॥
1413.6: Those who have forgotten the Naam, clinging to false greed, (theirs is) the toil of enticing Maya (the world's illusion and lure), and the fire of craving within. Those whose vine bears no gourd have been cheated by Maya, the cheat. The manmukhs (the self-willed) are bound and driven off; like dogs, they do not join the herd. When he himself leads astray, one goes astray; he himself unites (one) in union. O Nanak, through the Guru one is released, if one walks in the True Guru's will. ॥6॥
1413.7: The praiseworthy (Lord) is to be praised; praise the True One again and again. O Nanak, the one door (of the Lord) is true; the second should be abandoned. ॥7॥
1413.8: Wherever I, Nanak, wander, there is the True One; wherever I look, there is the One; through the Guru he becomes manifest. ॥8॥
1413.9: The Shabad (the Word) takes away sorrow, if someone keeps it in the mind; through the Guru's grace it comes to dwell in the mind; it is received by (the Lord's) grace. ॥9॥
1413.10: O Nanak, saying I, I, hosts beyond count, hundreds of thousands, have wasted away and died; those who met the True Guru were saved, through the True Shabad of the unseen (Lord). ॥10॥
1413.11: Those who have served the True Guru with one mind: I fall at the feet of such ones. Through the Guru's Shabad the Lord comes to dwell in the mind, and the hunger for Maya goes. Pure and radiant are those people who, through the Guru, merge in the Naam. O Nanak, other kingdoms are false; those dyed in the Naam are the (true) kings. ॥11॥
1413.12: As in a husband's home a devoted wife longs intensely (to serve him) with loving devotion, and prepares dishes of many flavours, adding the six delicious tastes, so the devotees praise (the Lord) through the Bani (the Guru's Word), fixing their minds on the Lord's Name. They have laid mind, body and wealth before (the Guru), and gone and sold their heads to the Guru. In reverent fear the devotees long greatly for devotion; God fulfils their longing and unites them (with himself). The Lord God is free of need: by what food is he satisfied? When one walks in the True Guru's will and sings of the Lord's virtues, (the Lord) is satisfied. Blessed, blessed in Kalyug (the dark age), O Nanak, are those who walk in the True Guru's will. ॥12॥
1414.1: They have not served the True Guru, nor kept the Shabad enshrined in the heart: cursed is their living; why did they come into the world? When through the Guru's teaching (the Lord's) fear enters the mind, then one is joined in love to the Lord's sweet essence. The Name is received as written from the beginning; O servant Nanak, (it) carries (one) across. ॥13॥
1414.2: In attachment to Maya the world has gone astray; the house is being robbed, and it is not aware. Lust and anger have stolen the mind; the manmukh is blind in the world. One who has slain the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) with the sword of (divine) wisdom stays awake through the Guru's teaching; the jewel of the Naam shines forth (in him), and his mind and body become pure. Those without the Naam wander about with their noses cut (in disgrace); without the Name one sits and weeps. O Nanak, what the Creator has written from the beginning, no one can erase. ॥14॥
1414.3: The Gurmukhs have earned the wealth of the Lord, reflecting on the Guru's Shabad; they have obtained the treasure of the Naam, and their storehouses are full and never run short. Through the Bani they utter the praises of the Lord, who has no end, no near shore and no far shore. O Nanak, the Creator brings about all causes, and the Maker watches over (all). ॥15॥
1414.4: Within the Gurmukh is Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise); his mind has risen to the tenth sky (the Tenth Gate). There is no drowsiness there, nor hunger; (there) is the Lord's Amrit Naam, an abode of peace. O Nanak, pain and pleasure do not touch (one) where there is the light of the all-pervading Lord (Atam Ram). ॥16॥
The Tenth Gate (dasam duar): the inner door beyond the body's nine openings, where the soul meets God.
1414.5: All have come (into the world) wearing round their necks the robe of lust and anger. Some are born, some perish; by (his) Hukam (God's will and command) one comes and goes. Birth and death do not end, for one is dyed in the love of another. Binding them in bonds, he has made them wander; nothing can be done (about it). ॥17॥
1414.6: Those on whom he has shown his grace: the True Guru has come and met them. Meeting the True Guru, (the mind) was turned around; dying (to self), one came alive, in Sahaj and in love. O Nanak, dyed in devotion, one merges in the Name of the Lord, Har Har. ॥18॥
1414.7: The manmukh's intellect is fickle; within him is much cleverness. All that he does goes in vain; not a particle is accepted. Whatever charity and giving they sow, it all goes to Dharam Raj (the judge of souls). Without the True Guru, Jamkaal (death) does not let go; in the love of another one is ruined. Youth slips away unseen; old age arrives, and one dies. There is attachment and love for son and wife, (but) at the end no one stands by as a friend or helper. One who serves the True Guru obtains peace, and the Name comes and dwells in his mind. O Nanak, great and greatly fortunate are those who, through the Guru, merge in the Naam. ॥19॥
1414.8: The manmukhs do not remember the Naam; without the Name one weeps in pain. They do not worship the all-pervading Lord; how can there be peace in the love of another? Within them is the filth of Haumai; they do not wash it out through the Shabad. O Nanak, without the Name, in their filth, they died, having wasted the treasure of human birth. ॥20॥
1415.1: The manmukhs are deaf and blind; within (each) is the dwelling of fire. They do not grasp the Bani with their awareness, nor bring forth light through the Shabad. They have no awareness of their own inner self, and do not put their faith in the Guru's word. Within the wise is the Guru's Shabad; they are ever attuned to the Lord, and ever in bloom. The Lord keeps (the honour) of the wise; I am ever a sacrifice to them. Those who, through the Guru, serve the Lord: servant Nanak is their slave. ॥21॥
1415.2: Maya is a serpent, a snake; with its poison, Maya has coiled round the world. The antidote to the poison is the Lord's Name: put the Guru's Shabad, the Garur, into your mouth. Those for whom it was written from before: the True Guru has come and met them. Meeting the True Guru, one has become pure, and the poison of Haumai has vanished. The faces of the Gurmukhs are radiant; they win honour in the Lord's court. Servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice to those who walk in the True Guru's will. ॥22॥
Garur: a remedy against snake venom, named after Garuda, the bird who is the enemy of snakes; it was ground on a stone and taken by mouth.
1415.3: The True Guru, the great Being, is without enmity; ever in his heart he is attuned to the Lord. One who bears enmity towards the one without enmity sets a firebrand to his own house. Within him are anger and pride; night and day he burns, and ever suffers pain. Telling lie upon lie, they bark all the time; in the love of another they have (as if) eaten poison. For the sake of the poison, Maya, they wander, going from house to house and losing their honour, like a prostitute's son, whose father's name is lost. They do not call to mind the Name of the Lord, Har Har; it is the Creator himself who has led them astray. The Lord has shown his grace to the Gurmukhs; the separated servants he himself unites (with himself). To those who have fallen at the True Guru's feet, servant Nanak is a sacrifice. ॥23॥
1415.4: Those attached to the Naam are saved; without the Name they go to the city of Jam. O Nanak, without the Name there is no peace; having come, they depart, and repent. ॥24॥
1415.5: When those running about in anxiety came to rest, bliss arose in their minds. By the Guru's grace one understands; (then) the soul-bride sleeps free of care. Those for whom it was written from before: the Guru, Govind (the Lord of the universe), has met them. O Nanak, in Sahaj they remain united, and have found the Lord, the supreme bliss. ॥25॥
1415.6: Those who serve their True Guru, reflecting on the Guru's Shabad, who accept the True Guru's will, and keep the Lord's Name enshrined in the heart, are honoured here and hereafter; they are engaged in the trade of the Lord's Name. Through the Guru, by the Shabad, they are known in that True Court. True is their merchandise, true their provisions; within them is love and affection (for the Lord). Jamkaal does not come near them; the Creator himself has forgiven them. O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam are rich; the whole world besides is poor. ॥26॥
1416.1: The support of the Lord's servant is the Name of the Lord; without the Lord's Name there is no place, no shelter. Through the Guru's teaching the Name dwells in the mind, and one stays absorbed in Sahaj, ever in Sahaj. By great fortune they have meditated on the Naam; day and night they are in love (with it). Servant Nanak begs for the dust (of the feet) of such ones: I am ever a sacrifice (to them). ॥27॥
1416.2: The earth with its eighty-four lakh forms of life, burning in craving, cries out. This attachment to Maya has spread over all, (yet) it does not go along at the last moment. Without the Lord peace does not come; before whom shall I cry out? By great fortune (one who) found the True Guru came to understand the knowledge of Brahm. The fire of craving was all quenched, O servant Nanak, by enshrining the Lord in the heart. ॥28॥
1416.3: We commit many faults; they have no end, no near shore and no far shore. O Lord, have mercy and pardon (me): I am a sinner, a great wrongdoer. O dear Lord, by the reckoning (of my deeds) my turn would never come; you are the one who forgives and unites (me with you). When the Guru is pleased, he unites (one) with the Lord God, cutting away all sins and vices. Those who have meditated on the Name of the Lord, Har Har: O servant Nanak, to them is acclaim. ॥29॥
1416.4: Those who, after separation upon separation, have been united, through fear and love of the True Guru, have become steady, (free) of birth and death, meditating on the Naam through the Guru. Joining the company of the Guru, the Saadh (the holy one), they find diamonds and jewels. O Nanak, the priceless ruby the Gurmukhs search out and find. ॥30॥
1416.5: The manmukh has not remembered the Naam: cursed is his life, cursed his dwelling (in the world). He whose gift is (his) food and clothing, that treasure of virtues, has not dwelt in his mind. This mind has not been pierced by the Shabad; how can it dwell in its own home? The manmukh brides are the forsaken ones; they die in coming and going. For the Gurmukhs, the Naam is their wedded happiness; on their foreheads the jewel (of good fortune) is written. They have enshrined the Name of the Lord, Har Har, in the heart; through the Lord, the lotus of the heart blossoms. They serve their True Guru; I am ever a sacrifice to them. O Nanak, radiant are the faces of those within whom is the light of the Naam. ॥31॥
1416.6: One who dies (to self) through the Shabad, that person alone succeeds; without the Shabad there is no liberation. They put on religious garbs and do many rites, and are ruined; in the love of another the people are ruined. O Nanak, the Name is not found without the True Guru, though one long for it a hundred times. ॥32॥
1416.7: The Lord's Name is very great and lofty, the loftiest of the lofty; none can reach it, though one long for it a hundred times. By (talk of) self-restraint with the mouth no one becomes good; everyone wanders about putting on religious garbs. One climbs (to him) by the Guru's ladder, which is obtained by (his) grace. (The Lord) comes to dwell within one who reflects on the Guru's Shabad. O Nanak, when one dies through the Shabad, the mind is won over; in the True One is true renown. ॥33॥
1417.1: Attachment to Maya is an ocean of pain; (it is) poison, hard to cross, and cannot be crossed. Crying mine, mine, they have burned away and died; (their life) passes in Haumai. The manmukhs have neither this shore nor the other; they remain caught midway. What is written from the beginning must be lived out; nothing (else) can be done. Through the Guru's teaching the jewel of (divine) wisdom dwells in the mind, and all is seen to be Brahm, through love. O Nanak, by great fortune one boards the ship of the True Guru; those (who board it) he carries across the terrifying world-ocean. ॥34॥
1417.2: Apart from the True Guru there is no giver who gives the Lord's Name as (life's) support. By the Guru's grace the Name dwells in the mind, and remains enshrined in the heart for ever. Craving is quenched and there is fulfilment, through love of the Lord's Name. O Nanak, through the Guru (the Name) is obtained, when the Lord shows his grace. ॥35॥
1417.3: Without the Shabad the world has gone mad; nothing can be said (of it). Those whom the Lord has protected are saved; they remain attuned to the Shabad. O Nanak, the Creator, who has made this whole design, knows everything. ॥36॥
1417.4: Burnt offerings, sacrifices, all the pilgrimages: the pandits have grown weary reading the Puranas, (yet) the poison, attachment to Maya, is not removed; in Haumai is coming and going. When the True Guru is met, the filth is washed away, (once) one has meditated on the Lord, the all-wise Being. To those who have served the Lord God, Har Har, servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice. ॥37॥
1417.5: They think much of attachment to Maya, of many hopes, of greed and vices. The manmukh does not become steady; he dies and perishes in an instant. If there is great fortune, one meets the True Guru, and gives up Haumai and vices. Repeating the Lord's Name and reflecting on the Shabad, O servant Nanak, they have found peace. ॥38॥
1417.6: Without the True Guru there is no devotion, nor is love for the Naam awakened. O servant Nanak, the Naam is worshipped in love and affection for the Guru. ॥39॥
1417.7: One should not trust a greedy person, as far as one can help it; at the last moment he deceives (one) there, where no one can lend a hand. One who keeps company with a manmukh gets his face stained with blackness. Black are the faces of those greedy ones; they will depart having wasted their lives. O Lord God, unite (me) with the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), that the Lord's Name may come to dwell in the mind, (and) the filth of birth and death be washed away, O servant Nanak, singing the Lord's praises. ॥40॥
1417.8: What the Lord God, the Creator, has written from the beginning cannot be erased. Soul and body are all his; the Sovereign Lord sustains (all). The backbiters and slanderers, hungry (for Maya), have died wretchedly; their hand reaches nowhere. Outwardly they do all their deeds in hypocrisy, practising deceit in mind and heart. Whatever is sown in the field of the body comes and stands (before one) at the end. O God, this is Nanak's prayer: O Lord, as it pleases you, forgive and unite (me with you). ॥41॥
1418.1: O mind, you do not see (your) coming and going, nor do you see the (Lord's) court. You are wrapped in attachment to Maya; within is ignorance, pitch darkness. The sleeping man awoke only then, when a heavy club struck his head. The Gurmukhs who have remembered the Lord at every moment find the door of liberation. O Nanak, they themselves are saved, and all their kin and family cross over (too). ॥42॥
1418.2: One who dies through the Shabad is known as truly dead (to self). By the Guru's grace he is satisfied with the Lord's sweet essence; in the Lord's court he is recognised through the Guru's Shabad. Without the Shabad everyone is dead; the manmukh is dead, having wasted his life. Those who do not remember the Lord's Name weep in pain at the end. O Nanak, that happens which the Creator does. ॥43॥
1418.3: The Gurmukhs, within whom are awareness and wisdom, never grow old; for ever and ever they dwell on the Lord's virtues, and within them is meditation in Sahaj. They abide ever in bliss and discernment, the same in sorrow and in joy. The One alone comes into their sight; everywhere they recognise the all-pervading Lord. ॥44॥
1418.4: The manmukh, even as a child, is like the old: (such are) those within whom there is no awareness of the Lord. They do their deeds in Haumai, and all go into the hands of Dharam Raj. The Gurmukhs are good and pure, (abiding) through the Guru's Shabad in (his) love. Not a speck of filth clings to those who walk in the True Guru's will. The manmukh's defilement does not come off, though he try a hundred washings. O Nanak, the Gurmukhs he has united (with himself), merging (them) in the Guru's embrace. ॥45॥
1418.5: One who does evil: how can he succeed? He burns himself in his own rage. The manmukh, crazed, chafes and quarrels. One who becomes Gurmukh understands everything. O Nanak, the Gurmukh wrestles with his own mind. ॥46॥
1418.6: Those who have not served the True Guru, the Being, nor reflected through the Shabad, are not to be called human: they are beasts, cattle, fools. Within them is neither wisdom nor meditation, nor any love or affection for the Lord. The manmukhs die in vice; again and again they die and are born. Those who meet the living come to live, enshrining in the heart the Lord, the life of the world. O Nanak, the Gurmukhs look beautiful in that true court. ॥47॥
1418.7: The Lord has built the temple of the Lord (the body), the temple in which the Lord dwells. Through the Guru's teaching, burning away attachment to Maya, (one) has found the Lord. In the Lord's temple are countless treasures; cherish the Naam, the nine treasures. Blessed and fortunate are they, O Nanak, who through the Guru have searched and found the Lord. By great fortune (they) have searched the fortress, the temple (of the body), and found the Lord with them, in the heart. ॥48॥
1418.8: The manmukhs roam in the ten directions, (driven by) overwhelming craving, greed and vice. Their attachment to Maya does not end; again and again they die and are born. Serving the True Guru and giving up overwhelming craving and vice, (one) has found peace. The pain of birth and death is gone, O servant Nanak, by reflecting on the Shabad. ॥49॥
1419.1: Meditate, O mind, on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (and you) will gain honour in the Lord's court. All misdeeds and sins are cut away, and the pride of Haumai comes to an end. Through the Guru the lotus (of the heart) blossoms, and the Supreme Self is recognised everywhere. O Lord, Har Har, O God, show mercy, (that) servant Nanak may repeat the Lord's Name. ॥50॥
1419.2: Dhanasri should be counted wealthy, O brother, only when (through it the soul-bride) does the True Guru's work; (when) she hands over body and mind, together with her soul, O brother, and moves as (his) Hukam directs. Where (the Lord) seats us, there we sit, O brother; where he sends me, there I go. No other wealth is as great, O brother, as the True Name. I sing for ever the virtues of the True One, O brother; I abide for ever with the True One. (One whose) clothing is virtues and good deeds, O brother, enjoys for himself the savour of his honour. What praise should one give him, O brother? He is a sacrifice to the sight of (the Lord). In the True Guru are great glories, O brother; (one) obtains them when (the Guru) is met by (the Lord's) grace. Some do not know how to obey the Hukam, O brother; they are made to wander in the love of another. They find no refuge in the Sangat, O brother, and get no place to sit. O Nanak, (the Lord) will make those obey the Hukam, O brother, who have earned the Name from the very first. I am devoted to them, O brother; to them I am ever a sacrifice. ॥51॥
Dhanasri is the raag's own name; the line plays on dhan, wealth.
1419.3: Those beards are true that bow at the Guru's feet; night and day they serve their Guru, and night and day abide in bliss. O Nanak, those faces look beautiful at the door of the True One. ॥52॥
1419.4: Those who speak the Truth and live the Truth: their faces are true, true their beards. The true Shabad has come to dwell in their minds, and they merge in the True Guru. Their capital is true, their wealth true; they attain the highest state. They hear the Truth, accept the Truth, and do the true work. They have a seat in the true court, and merge in the True One. O Nanak, without the True Guru one does not find the Truth; the manmukhs go astray. ॥53॥
1419.5: The rain-bird cries priu, priu (Beloved, Beloved), out of love and longing for the ocean of water (the cloud). Meeting the Guru, (the seeker) has found the cooling water, which takes away all sorrows. (His) thirst comes to an end, Sahaj wells up, and the crying and wailing end. O Nanak, through the Guru there is peace; keep the Naam enshrined in the heart. ॥54॥

The babiha (rain-bird, the pied cuckoo) is held in Indian poetry to drink only the raindrop that falls under the Swati star, and no other water, and to cry out for it; its cry is heard as priu (Beloved).
1419.6: O rain-bird, utter the True (Name), and fix your attention on the True One. Your call will be accepted: become Gurmukh and utter (the Name). Thirst is quenched by realising the Shabad: accept (the Lord's) will. (The cloud) rains in torrents on all four sides; the drop falls in Sahaj and in love. From water alone all comes forth; without water thirst does not go. O Nanak, one who has drunk the water of the Lord: no hunger comes to him. ॥55॥
1420.1: O rain-bird, speak in Sahaj, (steeped) in the true Shabad, in love. Everything is with you; the True Guru has shown (it to you). (If) you recognise your own self, the Beloved is met, and (the cloud) pours down in a downpour. Softly, drop by drop, the Amrit rains down, and all thirst and hunger go. There is no more crying and wailing, and the light is merged in the Light. O Nanak, merged in the True Name, the happy soul-brides sleep in peace. ॥56॥
1420.2: The Master has sent (the cloud) from on high, dispatching it by his true Hukam. Indra, in mercy, sends down the rain, pouring in a heavy downpour. There is peace in the rain-bird's body and mind when the drop of essence falls into its mouth. Grain and wealth spring up in plenty, and the earth is made beautiful. Night and day the people perform devotion, merged in the Guru's Shabad. The True One himself forgives, and in his grace works his will. Sing the Lord's virtues, O soul-bride, merged in the true Shabad. Make the Sahaj that comes from (his) fear your adornment, and stay lovingly attuned to the True One. O Nanak, (in whose) mind the Name alone dwells, the Lord sets (him) free in his court. ॥57॥
Indra: in the Puranas, the king of the gods, who sends the rain.
1420.3: O rain-bird, (even) if you roam the whole earth and fly up into the sky, (it is) when the True Guru is met that one finds the water, and hunger and thirst come to an end. Soul and body, all is his; everything is in his hands. Without being told, he knows everything; before whom (else) should one pray? O Nanak, the One pervades every heart; through the Shabad he gives light. ॥58॥
1420.4: O Nanak, it is spring for one who, serving the True Guru, stays merged (in the Lord). When the Lord pours down (his grace), mind and body all blossom, and the whole world turns green. ॥59॥
1420.5: Through the Shabad it is ever spring, by which body and mind turn green. O Nanak, (such a one) does not forget the Name of the One who created everyone. ॥60॥
1420.6: O Nanak, it is spring for those in whose minds, through the Guru, he has come to dwell. When the Lord pours down (his grace), mind and body blossom, and the whole world turns green. ॥61॥
1420.7: In the early dawn, whose beautiful Name should one take? One should take the Name of the Supreme God, who has the power to break and to make. ॥62॥
1420.8: Even the Persian wheels cry tu, tu (you, you), and speak with a sweet voice. The Master is ever present; why do you cry out so loud? (I am) a sacrifice to the Lord, who created the world and made this play. If you give up your self, then the Husband is met: this is the true understanding. Speech spoken in Haumai is insipid; (by it) I cannot understand (the Lord's) work. The forest, the grass and the three worlds meditate on you; night and day, always, (their time) passes so. Without the True Guru no one has found (you); (people) have grown weary of reflecting again and again. If you cast your glance of grace, you yourself set (them) right. O Nanak, those who have meditated (on you) through the Guru: approved is their coming (into the world). ॥63॥
1421.1: Yoga is not in saffron robes; yoga is not in dirty garb. O Nanak, sitting at home one attains yoga, through the True Guru's teaching. ॥64॥
1421.2: Even if you roam the four directions and read the Vedas through all four ages, O Nanak, (it is when) the True One is met and the Lord dwells in the mind that you will find the door of liberation. ॥65॥
1421.3: O Nanak, the Master's Hukam prevails; (your) understanding has turned astray, and you wander with a fickle mind. Making friends with the manmukhs, O friend, how can you ask for peace? Befriend the Gurmukhs, and fix your mind on the True Guru. (Then) the root of birth and death is cut away, and then there is peace, O friend. ॥66॥
1421.4: The one gone astray, on whom he casts his glance of grace, he himself will instruct. O Nanak, one left outside (his) grace keeps wailing in lament. ॥67॥
1421.5: Saloks, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Greatly fortunate are the happy wives whom the Lord King has met through the Guru. The light within (them) shines forth; O Nanak, they merge in the Name. ॥1॥
1421.6: Praise, praise to the True Guru, the Being, who has known the True One; meeting him, thirst is quenched, and body and mind become cool. Praise, praise to the True Guru, the true Being, to whom everyone is alike. Praise, praise to the True Guru, free of enmity, to whom slander and praise are the same. Praise, praise to the True Guru, the all-wise, within whom is reflection on Brahm. Praise, praise to the True Guru, (the image of) the Formless One, who has no end, no near shore and no far shore. Praise, praise to the True Guru, who makes the True One firm (in the heart). O Nanak, praise, praise to the True Guru, from whom the Naam is received. ॥2॥
1421.7: The true song of joy of the Lord God is, through the Guru, the Name of Govind. Praising the Naam night and day, and repeating the Lord's Name, there is bliss in the mind. By great fortune (one) has found the Lord, the perfect, supreme Bliss. Servant Nanak has praised the Naam; never again will there be any break in (his) mind and body. ॥3॥
1421.8: I have love for the Beloved; how may I meet the dear friends? I search for those friends whom the True One has adorned. The True Guru is my friend; if he meets me, I would offer this mind to him. He tells me of the Husband, the Lord, the Friend, the Creator. Says Nanak, I was searching for my Husband; O True Guru, (you) have shown (him to be) with (me). ॥4॥
1421.9: I stand watching the road, that my friend may perhaps come to me. Is there someone who would bring (him), and today unite me in union with my Husband? Whoever shows me my Beloved, for him I would cut my soul into four pieces. O Nanak, when the Lord is merciful, he then unites (one) with the perfect Guru. ॥5॥
1422.1: Within is the force of Haumai, in the body Maya; (such a one) comes and goes in falsehood. He cannot obey the True Guru's command, and the hard-to-cross (world-ocean) cannot be crossed. One on whom (the Lord) casts his glance of grace walks in the True Guru's will. The sight of the True Guru bears fruit: whatever one wishes, that fruit one obtains. Those who have put their faith in the True Guru: I fall at their feet. Nanak is the servant of one who, night and day, stays lovingly attuned (to him). ॥6॥
1422.2: Those who have love for the Beloved: how can they be satisfied without (his) sight? O Nanak, (when) they meet (him) in love, through the Guru this mind rejoices. ॥7॥
1422.3: Those who have love for the Beloved: how can they live apart from the Husband? When they see their Husband, O Nanak, they become green again. ॥8॥
1422.4: Those within whom, through the Guru, you, O true Beloved, have planted love, night and day, O Nanak, stay merged in love. ॥9॥
1422.5: Through the Guru comes true love, by which one finds the true Beloved; night and day they abide in bliss; O Nanak, one stays merged in Sahaj. ॥10॥
1422.6: From the perfect Guru one obtains true love and affection; it never breaks; O Nanak, one should sing the Lord's virtues. ॥11॥
1422.7: Those within whom is true love: how can they live without the Beloved? Through the Guru, O Nanak, he himself unites those long separated. ॥12॥
1422.8: Those in whom you yourself, showing (your) grace, have planted love and affection: Says Nanak, unite (me with you); give me, a beggar, the Name, O Lord. ॥13॥
1422.9: The Gurmukh laughs, the Gurmukh weeps; whatever the Gurmukh does, that is devotion. One who becomes Gurmukh reflects (on the Lord). The Gurmukh, O Nanak, reaches the far shore. ॥14॥
1422.10: Those within whom is the treasure of the Naam, by reflecting on the Gurbani: their faces are ever radiant in that true court. Sitting or standing, those whom the Creator himself has forgiven never forget (him). O Nanak, those united through the Guru, whom the Creator has united, are not parted. ॥15॥
1422.11: Service of the Guru-Pirs (the spiritual guides) is very hard, (yet it is) the most excellent peace. On whom he casts his glance of grace, in him he instils love and affection. Attached to the service of the True Guru, the world crosses the terrifying world-ocean. (Such a one) will obtain the fruit the mind longs for, and within (him) is discerning reflection. O Nanak, when the True Guru is met, one finds God, who takes away all sorrow. ॥16॥
1422.12: The manmukh who does service, with his mind set on the love of another: (to him) son, wife and family are (all), and he increases attachment to Maya. In the Lord's court the account is called for; at the end no one can set (him) free. Without the Name all is sorrow; attachment to Maya brings pain. O Nanak, (one to whom) through the Guru (the Lord) has come into sight: all attachment to Maya falls away from him. ॥17॥
1423.1: The Gurmukh obeys the Husband's Hukam, and through the Hukam finds peace. He serves the Hukam, worships the Hukam, and stays merged in the Hukam. The Hukam is (his) fasting, vow, purity and self-restraint; (by it) he obtains the fruit the mind longs for. She is ever a happy wife who understands the Hukam and serves the True Guru, lovingly attuned. O Nanak, those on whom he shows his grace, he unites (with himself) through the Hukam. ॥18॥
1423.2: The poor manmukh (bride) does not understand the Hukam; she ever does her deeds in Haumai. Fasts, vows, purity, self-restraint and worship: (by such) hypocrisy doubt does not go. Within, they are impure, pierced through by attachment to Maya, like the elephant that, (after bathing,) throws dust over itself. They do not remember the One who created (them); without remembering (him), how can one find peace? O Nanak, the Creator made the world's expanse from the very first; (each) acts out what was written from before. ॥19॥
1423.3: Through the Guru faith has come and the mind is won over; serving night and day, (one) stays merged (in him). The True Guru, the Guru, is within (him); all worship (him), and all come to behold the True Guru's sight. One should put faith in the True Guru, supreme in reflection, meeting whom all thirst and hunger go. I am ever, ever a sacrifice to my Guru, who unites (me) with the True God. O Nanak, they have received true grace who have come and fallen at the Guru's feet. ॥20॥
1423.4: Those who have love for the Beloved: those friends are with me. Within and without I roam, yet I keep (the Lord) cherished in the heart. ॥21॥
1423.5: Those who have meditated with one mind and one heart, fixing their minds on the True Guru: their pain, hunger and the great disease of Haumai are gone; lovingly attuned, they have become free of fault. They sing (his) virtues, utter (his) virtues, and (each) sleeps merged in (his) virtues. O Nanak, (they) have found (him) through the perfect Guru; in Sahaj God has come and met (them). ॥22॥
1423.6: The manmukh is attached to Maya; no love for the Naam takes hold (of him). He practises falsehood, hoards falsehood, and makes falsehood his food. (The manmukhs) die heaping up the wealth of Maya, which is poison, and in the end it all turns to ashes. They perform rites and religious duties, ritual purity and self-restraint, (but) within them is greed, (and) vice. O Nanak, whatever the manmukh does is not accepted; in the Lord's court he is put to shame. ॥23॥
1423.7: Among all the raags that one is good, O brother, by which (the Lord) comes to dwell in the mind. Such raag and naad (melody and sound) are all true; their worth cannot be told. (The Lord) is beyond raag and naad; by these his Hukam cannot be understood. O Nanak, for those who understand the Hukam, (all) comes right; this understanding comes from the True Guru. Everything has come about from him, as is his will. ॥24॥
1424.1: In the True Guru is the Amrit Name; he utters the Amrit and has (others) utter it. Through the Guru's teaching (comes) the pure Name: meditate on the pure Name. The Amrit Bani is the essence; through the Guru it comes to dwell in the mind. The lotus of the heart blossoms, and the light is merged in the Light. O Nanak, he has brought the True Guru to those on whose foreheads good fortune was written from the very first. ॥25॥
1424.2: Within is the fire of craving; the manmukh's hunger does not go. Attachment and family are all false; he stays entangled in the false. Night and day he broods on his worries; bound by worry he departs. His birth and death do not end, (as) he does his deeds in Haumai. In the Guru's refuge he is saved; O Nanak, (the Guru) sets (him) free. ॥26॥
1424.3: The True Guru, the Being, meditates on the Lord; the Sat Sangat (abides) in the True Guru's love. Those who serve the True Guru in the Sat Sangat, the Lord, through the Guru, unites with himself. This world and universe is a terrifying ocean; the Guru is the ship that carries (us) across by the Name. The Guru's Sikhs have accepted (his) will; the perfect Guru carries (them) across. O Lord, grant (us) the dust of the Guru's Sikhs, that we sinners too may attain salvation. O Nanak, (the one on whose) forehead the Lord God wrote (it) from the beginning has come and met the Guru. He (the Guru) has beaten and destroyed Jam's servants, and sets (him) free in the Lord's court. Acclaim to the Guru's Sikhs: the Lord, well pleased, has united them in union (with himself). ॥27॥
1424.4: The perfect Guru, who has driven out doubt from within, has made the Lord's Name firm (in a person). Singing the Name of Ram and the Lord's praise, and making it a light, (the Guru) has shown him the way. Having slain Haumai, he is lovingly attuned to the One, and has enshrined the Naam within. Through the Guru's teaching Jam cannot even cast an eye on him; he has merged in the True Name. The Creator himself is at work in all; whoever pleases him, he attaches to the Name. Servant Nanak lives when he takes the Name; without the Name, in an instant he dies. ॥28॥
1424.5: Within the mind is the disease of Haumai; through Haumai the Saakats, the wicked, are lost in doubt. O Nanak, meet the True Guru, the Saadh, the friend, and be rid of this disease. ॥29॥
1424.6: (The soul-bride who) through the Guru's teaching utters the Lord's Name, Har Har, drawn by the Lord's love, is steeped in the Lord day and night, her robe (the body) dyed in the Lord's colour. No being like the Lord is to be found; I have searched the whole world and seen it. The Name has been made firm (in me) by the Guru, the True Guru; (my) mind does not waver towards anything else. Servant Nanak is the Lord's slave, and of the Guru, the True Guru, the slave of slaves. ॥30॥
1425.1: Saloks, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Those who do not turn their faces away, who have come to know the Master: they alone are dyed (in his love). The unripe lovers, for whom (love) did not take effect, fall away again and again. ॥1॥
1425.2: Without the Master, silks and satins I have burnt in the fire; says Nanak, rolling in the dust I look beautiful, O Husband, (when I am) with you. ॥2॥
1425.3: Through the Guru's Shabad one should worship (the Lord); through the Naam and love comes detachment. The five enemies are conquered; O Nanak, (then) this Raag Maru is fruitful. ॥3॥
Maru here, and Sorath in the fifth salok, are the raags' own names.
1425.4: When I have the One, then (I have) a hundred thousand; those like you go begging at so many doors. (Even) a birth as a Brahmin has passed in vain, (when) the One who made (him) is forgotten. ॥4॥
By tradition, this salok was spoken to a Brahmin who, given alms by Guru Arjan Dev Ji, boasted that he had many other doors to beg at.
1425.5: In Sorath one should drink that essence which never turns insipid; O Nanak, the virtues of the Name of Ram should be sung: (by this comes) spotless glory in the Lord's court. ॥5॥
1425.6: Those whom God himself has protected, no one can kill. Within (such a one) is the treasure of the Naam; he ever cherishes (the Lord's) virtues. With the one support of the Inaccessible, he keeps God in mind and body. The colour of boundless love has taken hold (of him); no one can remove it. Through the Guru he sings the Lord's virtues and enjoys peace in Sahaj. O Nanak, he keeps the treasure of the Naam enshrined in his heart, deep within. ॥6॥
1425.7: Whatever (he) does, accept it as good; put away every other reckoning. (O Lord,) look (on me) with your glance of grace, and attach (me to you) yourself. Give your servant understanding and teaching, that doubt may go from within. The writ written from the start: that alone do all act out. Everything is in his power; there is no other place. O Nanak, accepting God's will, there is peace and bliss. ॥7॥
1425.8: Those who have remembered the perfect Guru, they alone have been made joyful. O Nanak, the Name is to be worshipped; (by it life's) purpose is fulfilled. ॥8॥
1425.9: The sinners do (evil) deeds and cry alas, alas; O Nanak, as the churning-sticks churn (the curd), so Dharam Raj churns (them). ॥9॥
1425.10: Good friends meditate on the Naam and win the priceless human birth; O Nanak, those who utter such dharma (the Name) have made the world holy. ॥10॥
1425.11: She who takes evil counsel is stuck in a foul place, (where) the mire (seems) sweet; O Nanak, they alone are saved who have good fortune on their foreheads. ॥11॥
1425.12: Those steeped in (the love of) their Husband sleep in peace; (those) parted in love from the Master cry out through all eight pahars. ॥12॥
1425.13: Countless sleep for the sake of false Maya; O Nanak, they are awake who utter the Naam with the tongue. ॥13॥
1425.14: Seeing the mirage and the peopled cities of the gandharvas, (people) go astray; those who have worshipped the True One, O Nanak, are beautiful in mind and body. ॥14॥

Mrig trishna (the deer's thirst): the mirage of water on hot sand, which the thirsty deer runs after. The city of the gandharvas (the city of Harichand): a city seen in the sky, a mirage that vanishes as one draws near.
1425.15: The Supreme Lord is the uplifter of the fallen, the all-powerful, infinite Being; whom he saves, O Nanak, that one remembers the Creator. ॥15॥
1426.1: Leave the other, crooked path, and fix your mind on the One; in other loves, O Nanak, (the soul-bride) is swept away in the current. ॥16॥
1426.2: In the market of three shops (the three qualities of Maya), the traders do their dealing; the true dealers are those who have loaded the merchandise of Truth. ॥17॥
1426.3: The foolish (soul-bride) does not know the path of love; she wanders astray. O Nanak, forgetting the Lord, (people) fall into dark hell. ॥18॥
1426.4: Maya is not forgotten by (his) mind; he begs for money and more money. That God does not come into (his) mind; O Nanak, it is not in his lot. ॥19॥
1426.5: (The wealth) never runs out at all, as long as he himself is merciful. The Shabad is inexhaustible, O brother; O Nanak, eat and spend (this) wealth and riches. ॥20॥
1426.6: Were I to find wings on sale, I would take them, (paying) an equal weight (of myself); I would set them on my own body and, searching, find that Friend. ॥21॥
1426.7: The Friend is the true Emperor, the King over the heads of kings; sitting near him one is adorned; he is the trust of all. ॥22॥

1410.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Salok Varan te Vadhik (the saloks beyond the vaars): by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(A young bride,) tall, full-bosomed, grave and full of pride, (says to her friend):
How shall I bow to my mother-in-law? I cannot bend, because of my breasts.
(The friend replies:) O friend, the mansions that stood like mountains, plastered with lime,
those too I have seen falling; O young woman, take no pride in your breasts. ॥1॥
1410.2: Listen, O young woman with eyes like a deer's, to a word deep and boundless:
having first recognised the goods well, only then should one make the deal.
One should raise the cry against the wicked, and acclaim for the friends;
O young woman, reflect on that cry through which the friends are met.
Body and mind should be given to the friends: such joy is the most excellent.
One should not set one's love on what is plainly passing away.
Nanak is a sacrifice to those who have understood it in this way. ॥2॥
1410.3: If you would be a swimmer of the waters, ask those who know the art of swimming across;
they are the truly wise: (with them) I would pass through these waves (of the world-ocean). ॥3॥
1410.4: Downpours, gales and floods, and waves by the hundred thousand are surging;
call out to the True Guru, and there is no fear of the boat sinking. ॥4॥
1410.5: O Nanak, what has the world become!
No guide on the path, no friend, has remained.
Love among brothers and kin has been done away with;
for the world's sake (people) have thrown away their faith. ॥5॥
1410.6: (At a death, people) cry alas, alas, and wail aloud;
they beat their cheeks and tear (the hair of) their heads.
Those who take the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) and keep patience (in his will):
Nanak is a sacrifice to them. ॥6॥
1410.7: O mind, one should not waver on the crooked (path): run on the straight path.
Behind is a fearsome tiger, ahead a lake of fire;
my soul is caught in dread, and I have no other way.
O Nanak, through the Guru one is released, and finds company with the Beloved Lord. ॥7॥
1410.8: The tiger dies and the mind is subdued in one who has the True Guru's teaching;
he recognises his own self, meets the Lord, and does not die again.
His hand does not sink into the mud, (when the Lord) beholds (him) with a single glance of grace.
O Nanak, the Gurmukhs (those who follow the Guru) are saved: the Guru is the lake, and the true embankment. ॥8॥
1411.1: Seek and find the water, (and) the fire dies out; (but) without the Guru, the treasure-house, there is no water.
(Without it) one is born and dies and is made to wander, even if (people) perform a hundred thousand rites.
Jam (the messenger of Death), the toll-collector, does not touch one who walks in the True Guru's will.
O Nanak, (his is) the stainless, deathless state: the Guru unites (him) in union with the Lord. ॥9॥
1411.2: In a little pond of brackish earth the crow bathes, scrubbing and scrubbing;
(yet) its mind and body are filthy with faults, and its beak is filled with stench.
In the company of crows, those foul birds, the swan did not know the lake (for what it is).
Such is love with a Saakat (one who has turned from God); understand this, O wise ones, in (the Lord's) love.
Hail the assembly of the Sants (saints), and do (your) deeds through the Guru:
O Nanak, this is the pure bathing: the Guru is the pilgrimage-place and the river. ॥10॥
1411.3: What shall I count as the fruit of being born, when there is no devotion to the Lord, no love?
What is worn and eaten is wasted, when in the mind is the love of another;
seeing and hearing are false, and false is the speech of the mouth.
O Nanak, praise the Naam; all else is Haumai (ego), coming and going. ॥11॥
1411.4: (Such people) are few, not many; the world is all show and coarse talk. ॥12॥
1411.5: O Nanak, one whom (the blow of love) strikes dies at once; no strength to live remains.
One who dies by the blow: that stroke is accepted.
It strikes the one whom (the Lord) strikes; then (only) is the stroke accepted.
The arrow of love does not come out, once that all-wise one has shot it. ॥13॥
1411.6: Who can wash the vessel that was made unbaked?
Mixing the five elements, a false show has been put together.
When it pleases him, (he) will set the vessel right;
awakening the Supreme Light, he will play the instrument (within). ॥14॥
1411.7: Those who are pitch-blind in mind do not know their duty, even when told.
With the mind blind and the lotus (of the heart) upturned, they look utterly hideous.
Some know how to speak and understand what is said: those men are wise and comely.
Some have no feel for music, nor for the Vedas, nor the delight of song; they do not know the sweet from the bitter.
Some have no success, no understanding, no grasp of sense, and do not know the mystery of the letters.
O Nanak, those men are truly donkeys who, without any virtue, take pride (in themselves). ॥15॥
1411.8: He is a Brahmin who knows Brahm (God),
who makes prayer, austerity and self-restraint his deeds,
who keeps to the dharma of gentleness and contentment,
who breaks his bonds and becomes free:
such a Brahmin alone is worthy of worship. ॥16॥
1411.9: He is a Khatri (of the warrior caste) who is a hero in (good) deeds,
who makes his body (an instrument) of charity and giving,
who knows the field and sows the gift (in it):
such a Khatri is accepted in the Lord's court.
If he practises greed, avarice and falsehood,
he himself receives (the fruit of) what he has done. ॥17॥
1411.10: Do not heat the body as an oven is heated, nor burn the bones as firewood;
what wrong have the head and the feet done (you)? Cherish the Beloved within. ॥18॥
1412.1: The Husband (Lord) dwells in every heart; there is no heart without the Husband.
O Nanak, those are the happy soul-brides in whom, through the Guru, he becomes manifest. ॥19॥
1412.2: If you long to play the game of love,
place your head on your palm and come into my lane.
If one is to set foot on this path,
one should give one's head, and not hesitate. ॥20॥
1412.3: Friendship with the kiraars (those ever counting their gains) rests on falsehood, and its footing is false;
O Mula, it is not known where death will come. ॥21॥
1412.4: blind is their conduct, (theirs is) the love of another. ॥22॥
1412.5: Without the Guru (there is no) wisdom, without dharma (no) meditation;
without truth there is no credit, and not even the capital is left. ॥23॥
1412.6: (The Lord) sends man (into the world), and he rises and goes;
there is no joy in such a thing. ॥24॥
1412.7: Ram grieves; he gathers his armies, and within him is the strength of command;
an army of monkeys serves him, with boundless zeal for battle in mind and body;
the ten-headed (Ravan) carried off Sita, and Lachhman died through a curse.
O Nanak, the Creator is the one who does all: he makes and unmakes, and beholds (it all). ॥25॥
1412.8: Ramchand grieves in his mind for Sita and for Lachhman;
he called to mind Hanvantar (Hanuman), who had come (to him) through (destined) union.
The deluded demon (Ravan) does not understand that God has done (all) these things.
O Nanak, he is free of all need; what was written by past deeds is not erased (even) by Ram. ॥26॥
1412.9: The city of Lahore is poison, a havoc lasting a pahar and a quarter. ॥27॥
1412.10: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The city of Lahore is a pool of Amrit (the nectar of the Name), the home of (the Lord's) praises. ॥28॥
1412.11: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
What is the sign of prosperity? There is no shortage of grain;
prosperity has settled in the very house, (filled with) the clamour of girls and women;
the seven women in the house mourn and wail; they weep over false concerns;
what he takes he does not give (back); he earns his coins, (yet lives) in dread. ॥29॥
1412.12: O pool, you were all green, your lotuses the colour of gold;
by what fault were you scorched, and your fair body turned black? (It replies:) O Nanak, my body has suffered loss;
I know it: I do not find the water with which I had my companionship,
at whose sight the body blossoms and takes on a fourfold colour. ॥30॥
1412.13: No one has lived to his fill, and no one has left with (his tasks) completed.
The one with (divine) wisdom lives for ever and ever; honour comes only to the one whose awareness (is fixed on God).
In saving and sparing, ever and ever, (life) has passed away like this.
O Nanak, to whom should one complain? (Death) takes (one) away without even asking. ॥31॥
1412.14: Do not blame the Rai (the rich man): when he grows old, his understanding goes.
He talks a great deal, so the blind one must fall into pits and ditches. ॥32॥
1412.15: All that the Perfect One has done is perfect; there is nothing too little or too much (in it).
O Nanak, the Gurmukh knows it so; (such ones) merge in the Perfect One. ॥33॥
1413.1: Saloks, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Those are not to be called abhiagats (holy wanderers) in whose minds is restless wandering;
O Nanak, what is given to them earns merit just like them. ॥1॥
1413.2: One who becomes a beggar for the supreme state of the fearless, stainless (Lord):
O Nanak, rare is the one who is blessed to provide the food of such a one. ॥2॥
1413.3: Were I to become a pandit or an astrologer, or recite the four Vedas by heart,
(still) in the nine regions (of the earth) I would be known by my own conduct and thought. ॥3॥
1413.4: Killing a Brahmin or a cow, (killing) a daughter, (taking) the grain of an evil-doer,
curses upon curses, the leprosy of evil deeds, pride forever and ever:
all these are earned, O Nanak, by those who forget the one Naam;
all (other) cleverness is burnt away, and only the essence, (divine) wisdom, remains. ॥4॥
1413.5: What is written on the forehead from the beginning, no one can erase.
O Nanak, what is written comes to pass; he alone understands (this) on whom is (the Lord's) glance of grace. ॥5॥
1413.6: Those who have forgotten the Naam, clinging to false greed,
(theirs is) the toil of enticing Maya (the world's illusion and lure), and the fire of craving within.
Those whose vine bears no gourd have been cheated by Maya, the cheat.
The manmukhs (the self-willed) are bound and driven off; like dogs, they do not join the herd.
When he himself leads astray, one goes astray; he himself unites (one) in union.
O Nanak, through the Guru one is released, if one walks in the True Guru's will. ॥6॥
1413.7: The praiseworthy (Lord) is to be praised; praise the True One again and again.
O Nanak, the one door (of the Lord) is true; the second should be abandoned. ॥7॥
1413.8: Wherever I, Nanak, wander, there is the True One;
wherever I look, there is the One; through the Guru he becomes manifest. ॥8॥
1413.9: The Shabad (the Word) takes away sorrow, if someone keeps it in the mind;
through the Guru's grace it comes to dwell in the mind; it is received by (the Lord's) grace. ॥9॥
1413.10: O Nanak, saying I, I, hosts beyond count, hundreds of thousands, have wasted away and died;
those who met the True Guru were saved, through the True Shabad of the unseen (Lord). ॥10॥
1413.11: Those who have served the True Guru with one mind: I fall at the feet of such ones.
Through the Guru's Shabad the Lord comes to dwell in the mind, and the hunger for Maya goes.
Pure and radiant are those people who, through the Guru, merge in the Naam.
O Nanak, other kingdoms are false; those dyed in the Naam are the (true) kings. ॥11॥
1413.12: As in a husband's home a devoted wife longs intensely (to serve him) with loving devotion,
and prepares dishes of many flavours, adding the six delicious tastes,
so the devotees praise (the Lord) through the Bani (the Guru's Word), fixing their minds on the Lord's Name.
They have laid mind, body and wealth before (the Guru), and gone and sold their heads to the Guru.
In reverent fear the devotees long greatly for devotion; God fulfils their longing and unites them (with himself).
The Lord God is free of need: by what food is he satisfied?
When one walks in the True Guru's will and sings of the Lord's virtues, (the Lord) is satisfied.
Blessed, blessed in Kalyug (the dark age), O Nanak, are those who walk in the True Guru's will. ॥12॥
1414.1: They have not served the True Guru, nor kept the Shabad enshrined in the heart:
cursed is their living; why did they come into the world?
When through the Guru's teaching (the Lord's) fear enters the mind, then one is joined in love to the Lord's sweet essence.
The Name is received as written from the beginning; O servant Nanak, (it) carries (one) across. ॥13॥
1414.2: In attachment to Maya the world has gone astray; the house is being robbed, and it is not aware.
Lust and anger have stolen the mind; the manmukh is blind in the world.
One who has slain the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) with the sword of (divine) wisdom stays awake through the Guru's teaching;
the jewel of the Naam shines forth (in him), and his mind and body become pure.
Those without the Naam wander about with their noses cut (in disgrace); without the Name one sits and weeps.
O Nanak, what the Creator has written from the beginning, no one can erase. ॥14॥
1414.3: The Gurmukhs have earned the wealth of the Lord, reflecting on the Guru's Shabad;
they have obtained the treasure of the Naam, and their storehouses are full and never run short.
Through the Bani they utter the praises of the Lord, who has no end, no near shore and no far shore.
O Nanak, the Creator brings about all causes, and the Maker watches over (all). ॥15॥
1414.4: Within the Gurmukh is Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise); his mind has risen to the tenth sky (the Tenth Gate).
There is no drowsiness there, nor hunger; (there) is the Lord's Amrit Naam, an abode of peace.
O Nanak, pain and pleasure do not touch (one) where there is the light of the all-pervading Lord (Atam Ram). ॥16॥
1414.5: All have come (into the world) wearing round their necks the robe of lust and anger.
Some are born, some perish; by (his) Hukam (God's will and command) one comes and goes.
Birth and death do not end, for one is dyed in the love of another.
Binding them in bonds, he has made them wander; nothing can be done (about it). ॥17॥
1414.6: Those on whom he has shown his grace: the True Guru has come and met them.
Meeting the True Guru, (the mind) was turned around; dying (to self), one came alive, in Sahaj and in love.
O Nanak, dyed in devotion, one merges in the Name of the Lord, Har Har. ॥18॥
1414.7: The manmukh's intellect is fickle; within him is much cleverness.
All that he does goes in vain; not a particle is accepted.
Whatever charity and giving they sow, it all goes to Dharam Raj (the judge of souls).
Without the True Guru, Jamkaal (death) does not let go; in the love of another one is ruined.
Youth slips away unseen; old age arrives, and one dies.
There is attachment and love for son and wife, (but) at the end no one stands by as a friend or helper.
One who serves the True Guru obtains peace, and the Name comes and dwells in his mind.
O Nanak, great and greatly fortunate are those who, through the Guru, merge in the Naam. ॥19॥
1414.8: The manmukhs do not remember the Naam; without the Name one weeps in pain.
They do not worship the all-pervading Lord; how can there be peace in the love of another?
Within them is the filth of Haumai; they do not wash it out through the Shabad.
O Nanak, without the Name, in their filth, they died, having wasted the treasure of human birth. ॥20॥
1415.1: The manmukhs are deaf and blind; within (each) is the dwelling of fire.
They do not grasp the Bani with their awareness, nor bring forth light through the Shabad.
They have no awareness of their own inner self, and do not put their faith in the Guru's word.
Within the wise is the Guru's Shabad; they are ever attuned to the Lord, and ever in bloom.
The Lord keeps (the honour) of the wise; I am ever a sacrifice to them.
Those who, through the Guru, serve the Lord: servant Nanak is their slave. ॥21॥
1415.2: Maya is a serpent, a snake; with its poison, Maya has coiled round the world.
The antidote to the poison is the Lord's Name: put the Guru's Shabad, the Garur, into your mouth.
Those for whom it was written from before: the True Guru has come and met them.
Meeting the True Guru, one has become pure, and the poison of Haumai has vanished.
The faces of the Gurmukhs are radiant; they win honour in the Lord's court.
Servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice to those who walk in the True Guru's will. ॥22॥
1415.3: The True Guru, the great Being, is without enmity; ever in his heart he is attuned to the Lord.
One who bears enmity towards the one without enmity sets a firebrand to his own house.
Within him are anger and pride; night and day he burns, and ever suffers pain.
Telling lie upon lie, they bark all the time; in the love of another they have (as if) eaten poison.
For the sake of the poison, Maya, they wander, going from house to house and losing their honour,
like a prostitute's son, whose father's name is lost.
They do not call to mind the Name of the Lord, Har Har; it is the Creator himself who has led them astray.
The Lord has shown his grace to the Gurmukhs; the separated servants he himself unites (with himself).
To those who have fallen at the True Guru's feet, servant Nanak is a sacrifice. ॥23॥
1415.4: Those attached to the Naam are saved; without the Name they go to the city of Jam.
O Nanak, without the Name there is no peace; having come, they depart, and repent. ॥24॥
1415.5: When those running about in anxiety came to rest, bliss arose in their minds.
By the Guru's grace one understands; (then) the soul-bride sleeps free of care.
Those for whom it was written from before: the Guru, Govind (the Lord of the universe), has met them.
O Nanak, in Sahaj they remain united, and have found the Lord, the supreme bliss. ॥25॥
1415.6: Those who serve their True Guru, reflecting on the Guru's Shabad,
who accept the True Guru's will, and keep the Lord's Name enshrined in the heart,
are honoured here and hereafter; they are engaged in the trade of the Lord's Name.
Through the Guru, by the Shabad, they are known in that True Court.
True is their merchandise, true their provisions; within them is love and affection (for the Lord).
Jamkaal does not come near them; the Creator himself has forgiven them.
O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam are rich; the whole world besides is poor. ॥26॥
1416.1: The support of the Lord's servant is the Name of the Lord; without the Lord's Name there is no place, no shelter.
Through the Guru's teaching the Name dwells in the mind, and one stays absorbed in Sahaj, ever in Sahaj.
By great fortune they have meditated on the Naam; day and night they are in love (with it).
Servant Nanak begs for the dust (of the feet) of such ones: I am ever a sacrifice (to them). ॥27॥
1416.2: The earth with its eighty-four lakh forms of life, burning in craving, cries out.
This attachment to Maya has spread over all, (yet) it does not go along at the last moment.
Without the Lord peace does not come; before whom shall I cry out?
By great fortune (one who) found the True Guru came to understand the knowledge of Brahm.
The fire of craving was all quenched, O servant Nanak, by enshrining the Lord in the heart. ॥28॥
1416.3: We commit many faults; they have no end, no near shore and no far shore.
O Lord, have mercy and pardon (me): I am a sinner, a great wrongdoer.
O dear Lord, by the reckoning (of my deeds) my turn would never come; you are the one who forgives and unites (me with you).
When the Guru is pleased, he unites (one) with the Lord God, cutting away all sins and vices.
Those who have meditated on the Name of the Lord, Har Har: O servant Nanak, to them is acclaim. ॥29॥
1416.4: Those who, after separation upon separation, have been united, through fear and love of the True Guru,
have become steady, (free) of birth and death, meditating on the Naam through the Guru.
Joining the company of the Guru, the Saadh (the holy one), they find diamonds and jewels.
O Nanak, the priceless ruby the Gurmukhs search out and find. ॥30॥
1416.5: The manmukh has not remembered the Naam: cursed is his life, cursed his dwelling (in the world).
He whose gift is (his) food and clothing, that treasure of virtues, has not dwelt in his mind.
This mind has not been pierced by the Shabad; how can it dwell in its own home?
The manmukh brides are the forsaken ones; they die in coming and going.
For the Gurmukhs, the Naam is their wedded happiness; on their foreheads the jewel (of good fortune) is written.
They have enshrined the Name of the Lord, Har Har, in the heart; through the Lord, the lotus of the heart blossoms.
They serve their True Guru; I am ever a sacrifice to them.
O Nanak, radiant are the faces of those within whom is the light of the Naam. ॥31॥
1416.6: One who dies (to self) through the Shabad, that person alone succeeds; without the Shabad there is no liberation.
They put on religious garbs and do many rites, and are ruined; in the love of another the people are ruined.
O Nanak, the Name is not found without the True Guru, though one long for it a hundred times. ॥32॥
1416.7: The Lord's Name is very great and lofty, the loftiest of the lofty;
none can reach it, though one long for it a hundred times.
By (talk of) self-restraint with the mouth no one becomes good; everyone wanders about putting on religious garbs.
One climbs (to him) by the Guru's ladder, which is obtained by (his) grace.
(The Lord) comes to dwell within one who reflects on the Guru's Shabad.
O Nanak, when one dies through the Shabad, the mind is won over; in the True One is true renown. ॥33॥
1417.1: Attachment to Maya is an ocean of pain; (it is) poison, hard to cross, and cannot be crossed.
Crying mine, mine, they have burned away and died; (their life) passes in Haumai.
The manmukhs have neither this shore nor the other; they remain caught midway.
What is written from the beginning must be lived out; nothing (else) can be done.
Through the Guru's teaching the jewel of (divine) wisdom dwells in the mind, and all is seen to be Brahm, through love.
O Nanak, by great fortune one boards the ship of the True Guru; those (who board it) he carries across the terrifying world-ocean. ॥34॥
1417.2: Apart from the True Guru there is no giver who gives the Lord's Name as (life's) support.
By the Guru's grace the Name dwells in the mind, and remains enshrined in the heart for ever.
Craving is quenched and there is fulfilment, through love of the Lord's Name.
O Nanak, through the Guru (the Name) is obtained, when the Lord shows his grace. ॥35॥
1417.3: Without the Shabad the world has gone mad; nothing can be said (of it).
Those whom the Lord has protected are saved; they remain attuned to the Shabad.
O Nanak, the Creator, who has made this whole design, knows everything. ॥36॥
1417.4: Burnt offerings, sacrifices, all the pilgrimages: the pandits have grown weary reading the Puranas,
(yet) the poison, attachment to Maya, is not removed; in Haumai is coming and going.
When the True Guru is met, the filth is washed away, (once) one has meditated on the Lord, the all-wise Being.
To those who have served the Lord God, Har Har, servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice. ॥37॥
1417.5: They think much of attachment to Maya, of many hopes, of greed and vices.
The manmukh does not become steady; he dies and perishes in an instant.
If there is great fortune, one meets the True Guru, and gives up Haumai and vices.
Repeating the Lord's Name and reflecting on the Shabad, O servant Nanak, they have found peace. ॥38॥
1417.6: Without the True Guru there is no devotion, nor is love for the Naam awakened.
O servant Nanak, the Naam is worshipped in love and affection for the Guru. ॥39॥
1417.7: One should not trust a greedy person, as far as one can help it;
at the last moment he deceives (one) there, where no one can lend a hand.
One who keeps company with a manmukh gets his face stained with blackness.
Black are the faces of those greedy ones; they will depart having wasted their lives.
O Lord God, unite (me) with the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), that the Lord's Name may come to dwell in the mind,
(and) the filth of birth and death be washed away, O servant Nanak, singing the Lord's praises. ॥40॥
1417.8: What the Lord God, the Creator, has written from the beginning cannot be erased.
Soul and body are all his; the Sovereign Lord sustains (all).
The backbiters and slanderers, hungry (for Maya), have died wretchedly; their hand reaches nowhere.
Outwardly they do all their deeds in hypocrisy, practising deceit in mind and heart.
Whatever is sown in the field of the body comes and stands (before one) at the end.
O God, this is Nanak's prayer: O Lord, as it pleases you, forgive and unite (me with you). ॥41॥
1418.1: O mind, you do not see (your) coming and going, nor do you see the (Lord's) court.
You are wrapped in attachment to Maya; within is ignorance, pitch darkness.
The sleeping man awoke only then, when a heavy club struck his head.
The Gurmukhs who have remembered the Lord at every moment find the door of liberation.
O Nanak, they themselves are saved, and all their kin and family cross over (too). ॥42॥
1418.2: One who dies through the Shabad is known as truly dead (to self).
By the Guru's grace he is satisfied with the Lord's sweet essence;
in the Lord's court he is recognised through the Guru's Shabad.
Without the Shabad everyone is dead;
the manmukh is dead, having wasted his life.
Those who do not remember the Lord's Name weep in pain at the end.
O Nanak, that happens which the Creator does. ॥43॥
1418.3: The Gurmukhs, within whom are awareness and wisdom, never grow old;
for ever and ever they dwell on the Lord's virtues, and within them is meditation in Sahaj.
They abide ever in bliss and discernment, the same in sorrow and in joy.
The One alone comes into their sight; everywhere they recognise the all-pervading Lord. ॥44॥
1418.4: The manmukh, even as a child, is like the old: (such are) those within whom there is no awareness of the Lord.
They do their deeds in Haumai, and all go into the hands of Dharam Raj.
The Gurmukhs are good and pure, (abiding) through the Guru's Shabad in (his) love.
Not a speck of filth clings to those who walk in the True Guru's will.
The manmukh's defilement does not come off, though he try a hundred washings.
O Nanak, the Gurmukhs he has united (with himself), merging (them) in the Guru's embrace. ॥45॥
1418.5: One who does evil: how can he succeed?
He burns himself in his own rage.
The manmukh, crazed, chafes and quarrels.
One who becomes Gurmukh understands everything.
O Nanak, the Gurmukh wrestles with his own mind. ॥46॥
1418.6: Those who have not served the True Guru, the Being, nor reflected through the Shabad,
are not to be called human: they are beasts, cattle, fools.
Within them is neither wisdom nor meditation, nor any love or affection for the Lord.
The manmukhs die in vice; again and again they die and are born.
Those who meet the living come to live, enshrining in the heart the Lord, the life of the world.
O Nanak, the Gurmukhs look beautiful in that true court. ॥47॥
1418.7: The Lord has built the temple of the Lord (the body), the temple in which the Lord dwells.
Through the Guru's teaching, burning away attachment to Maya, (one) has found the Lord.
In the Lord's temple are countless treasures; cherish the Naam, the nine treasures.
Blessed and fortunate are they, O Nanak, who through the Guru have searched and found the Lord.
By great fortune (they) have searched the fortress, the temple (of the body), and found the Lord with them, in the heart. ॥48॥
1418.8: The manmukhs roam in the ten directions, (driven by) overwhelming craving, greed and vice.
Their attachment to Maya does not end; again and again they die and are born.
Serving the True Guru and giving up overwhelming craving and vice, (one) has found peace.
The pain of birth and death is gone, O servant Nanak, by reflecting on the Shabad. ॥49॥
