1419.1: Meditate, O mind, on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (and you) will gain honour in the Lord's court.
All misdeeds and sins are cut away, and the pride of Haumai comes to an end.
Through the Guru the lotus (of the heart) blossoms, and the Supreme Self is recognised everywhere.
O Lord, Har Har, O God, show mercy, (that) servant Nanak may repeat the Lord's Name. ॥50॥
1419.2: Dhanasri should be counted wealthy, O brother, only when (through it the soul-bride) does the True Guru's work;
(when) she hands over body and mind, together with her soul, O brother, and moves as (his) Hukam directs.
Where (the Lord) seats us, there we sit, O brother; where he sends me, there I go.
No other wealth is as great, O brother, as the True Name.
I sing for ever the virtues of the True One, O brother; I abide for ever with the True One.
(One whose) clothing is virtues and good deeds, O brother, enjoys for himself the savour of his honour.
What praise should one give him, O brother? He is a sacrifice to the sight of (the Lord).
In the True Guru are great glories, O brother; (one) obtains them when (the Guru) is met by (the Lord's) grace.
Some do not know how to obey the Hukam, O brother; they are made to wander in the love of another.
They find no refuge in the Sangat, O brother, and get no place to sit.
O Nanak, (the Lord) will make those obey the Hukam, O brother, who have earned the Name from the very first.
I am devoted to them, O brother; to them I am ever a sacrifice. ॥51॥
1419.3: Those beards are true that bow at the Guru's feet;
night and day they serve their Guru, and night and day abide in bliss.
O Nanak, those faces look beautiful at the door of the True One. ॥52॥
1419.4: Those who speak the Truth and live the Truth: their faces are true, true their beards.
The true Shabad has come to dwell in their minds, and they merge in the True Guru.
Their capital is true, their wealth true; they attain the highest state.
They hear the Truth, accept the Truth, and do the true work.
They have a seat in the true court, and merge in the True One.
O Nanak, without the True Guru one does not find the Truth; the manmukhs go astray. ॥53॥
1419.5: The rain-bird cries priu, priu (Beloved, Beloved), out of love and longing for the ocean of water (the cloud).
Meeting the Guru, (the seeker) has found the cooling water, which takes away all sorrows.
(His) thirst comes to an end, Sahaj wells up, and the crying and wailing end.
O Nanak, through the Guru there is peace; keep the Naam enshrined in the heart. ॥54॥
1419.6: O rain-bird, utter the True (Name), and fix your attention on the True One.
Your call will be accepted: become Gurmukh and utter (the Name).
Thirst is quenched by realising the Shabad: accept (the Lord's) will.
(The cloud) rains in torrents on all four sides; the drop falls in Sahaj and in love.
From water alone all comes forth; without water thirst does not go.
O Nanak, one who has drunk the water of the Lord: no hunger comes to him. ॥55॥
1420.1: O rain-bird, speak in Sahaj, (steeped) in the true Shabad, in love.
Everything is with you; the True Guru has shown (it to you).
(If) you recognise your own self, the Beloved is met, and (the cloud) pours down in a downpour.
Softly, drop by drop, the Amrit rains down, and all thirst and hunger go.
There is no more crying and wailing, and the light is merged in the Light.
O Nanak, merged in the True Name, the happy soul-brides sleep in peace. ॥56॥
1420.2: The Master has sent (the cloud) from on high, dispatching it by his true Hukam.
Indra, in mercy, sends down the rain, pouring in a heavy downpour.
There is peace in the rain-bird's body and mind when the drop of essence falls into its mouth.
Grain and wealth spring up in plenty, and the earth is made beautiful.
Night and day the people perform devotion, merged in the Guru's Shabad.
The True One himself forgives, and in his grace works his will.
Sing the Lord's virtues, O soul-bride, merged in the true Shabad.
Make the Sahaj that comes from (his) fear your adornment, and stay lovingly attuned to the True One.
O Nanak, (in whose) mind the Name alone dwells, the Lord sets (him) free in his court. ॥57॥
1420.3: O rain-bird, (even) if you roam the whole earth and fly up into the sky,
(it is) when the True Guru is met that one finds the water, and hunger and thirst come to an end.
Soul and body, all is his; everything is in his hands.
Without being told, he knows everything; before whom (else) should one pray?
O Nanak, the One pervades every heart; through the Shabad he gives light. ॥58॥
1420.4: O Nanak, it is spring for one who, serving the True Guru, stays merged (in the Lord).
When the Lord pours down (his grace), mind and body all blossom, and the whole world turns green. ॥59॥
1420.5: Through the Shabad it is ever spring, by which body and mind turn green.
O Nanak, (such a one) does not forget the Name of the One who created everyone. ॥60॥
1420.6: O Nanak, it is spring for those in whose minds, through the Guru, he has come to dwell.
When the Lord pours down (his grace), mind and body blossom, and the whole world turns green. ॥61॥
1420.7: In the early dawn, whose beautiful Name should one take?
One should take the Name of the Supreme God, who has the power to break and to make. ॥62॥
1420.8: Even the Persian wheels cry tu, tu (you, you), and speak with a sweet voice.
The Master is ever present; why do you cry out so loud?
(I am) a sacrifice to the Lord, who created the world and made this play.
If you give up your self, then the Husband is met: this is the true understanding.
Speech spoken in Haumai is insipid; (by it) I cannot understand (the Lord's) work.
The forest, the grass and the three worlds meditate on you; night and day, always, (their time) passes so.
Without the True Guru no one has found (you); (people) have grown weary of reflecting again and again.
If you cast your glance of grace, you yourself set (them) right.
O Nanak, those who have meditated (on you) through the Guru: approved is their coming (into the world). ॥63॥
1421.1: Yoga is not in saffron robes; yoga is not in dirty garb.
O Nanak, sitting at home one attains yoga, through the True Guru's teaching. ॥64॥
1421.2: Even if you roam the four directions and read the Vedas through all four ages,
O Nanak, (it is when) the True One is met and the Lord dwells in the mind that you will find the door of liberation. ॥65॥
1421.3: O Nanak, the Master's Hukam prevails; (your) understanding has turned astray, and you wander with a fickle mind.
Making friends with the manmukhs, O friend, how can you ask for peace?
Befriend the Gurmukhs, and fix your mind on the True Guru.
(Then) the root of birth and death is cut away, and then there is peace, O friend. ॥66॥
1421.4: The one gone astray, on whom he casts his glance of grace, he himself will instruct.
O Nanak, one left outside (his) grace keeps wailing in lament. ॥67॥
1421.5: Saloks, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Greatly fortunate are the happy wives whom the Lord King has met through the Guru.
The light within (them) shines forth; O Nanak, they merge in the Name. ॥1॥
1421.6: Praise, praise to the True Guru, the Being, who has known the True One;
meeting him, thirst is quenched, and body and mind become cool.
Praise, praise to the True Guru, the true Being, to whom everyone is alike.
Praise, praise to the True Guru, free of enmity, to whom slander and praise are the same.
Praise, praise to the True Guru, the all-wise, within whom is reflection on Brahm.
Praise, praise to the True Guru, (the image of) the Formless One, who has no end, no near shore and no far shore.
Praise, praise to the True Guru, who makes the True One firm (in the heart).
O Nanak, praise, praise to the True Guru, from whom the Naam is received. ॥2॥
1421.7: The true song of joy of the Lord God is, through the Guru, the Name of Govind.
Praising the Naam night and day, and repeating the Lord's Name, there is bliss in the mind.
By great fortune (one) has found the Lord, the perfect, supreme Bliss.
Servant Nanak has praised the Naam; never again will there be any break in (his) mind and body. ॥3॥
1421.8: I have love for the Beloved; how may I meet the dear friends?
I search for those friends whom the True One has adorned.
The True Guru is my friend; if he meets me, I would offer this mind to him.
He tells me of the Husband, the Lord, the Friend, the Creator.
Says Nanak, I was searching for my Husband; O True Guru, (you) have shown (him to be) with (me). ॥4॥
1421.9: I stand watching the road, that my friend may perhaps come to me.
Is there someone who would bring (him), and today unite me in union with my Husband?
Whoever shows me my Beloved, for him I would cut my soul into four pieces.
O Nanak, when the Lord is merciful, he then unites (one) with the perfect Guru. ॥5॥
1422.1: Within is the force of Haumai, in the body Maya; (such a one) comes and goes in falsehood.
He cannot obey the True Guru's command, and the hard-to-cross (world-ocean) cannot be crossed.
One on whom (the Lord) casts his glance of grace walks in the True Guru's will.
The sight of the True Guru bears fruit: whatever one wishes, that fruit one obtains.
Those who have put their faith in the True Guru: I fall at their feet.
Nanak is the servant of one who, night and day, stays lovingly attuned (to him). ॥6॥
1422.2: Those who have love for the Beloved: how can they be satisfied without (his) sight?
O Nanak, (when) they meet (him) in love, through the Guru this mind rejoices. ॥7॥
1422.3: Those who have love for the Beloved: how can they live apart from the Husband?
When they see their Husband, O Nanak, they become green again. ॥8॥
1422.4: Those within whom, through the Guru, you, O true Beloved, have planted love,
night and day, O Nanak, stay merged in love. ॥9॥
1422.5: Through the Guru comes true love, by which one finds the true Beloved;
night and day they abide in bliss; O Nanak, one stays merged in Sahaj. ॥10॥
1422.6: From the perfect Guru one obtains true love and affection;
it never breaks; O Nanak, one should sing the Lord's virtues. ॥11॥
1422.7: Those within whom is true love: how can they live without the Beloved?
Through the Guru, O Nanak, he himself unites those long separated. ॥12॥
1422.8: Those in whom you yourself, showing (your) grace, have planted love and affection:
Says Nanak, unite (me with you); give me, a beggar, the Name, O Lord. ॥13॥
1422.9: The Gurmukh laughs, the Gurmukh weeps;
whatever the Gurmukh does, that is devotion.
One who becomes Gurmukh reflects (on the Lord).
The Gurmukh, O Nanak, reaches the far shore. ॥14॥
1422.10: Those within whom is the treasure of the Naam, by reflecting on the Gurbani:
their faces are ever radiant in that true court.
Sitting or standing, those whom the Creator himself has forgiven never forget (him).
O Nanak, those united through the Guru, whom the Creator has united, are not parted. ॥15॥
1422.11: Service of the Guru-Pirs (the spiritual guides) is very hard, (yet it is) the most excellent peace.
On whom he casts his glance of grace, in him he instils love and affection.
Attached to the service of the True Guru, the world crosses the terrifying world-ocean.
(Such a one) will obtain the fruit the mind longs for, and within (him) is discerning reflection.
O Nanak, when the True Guru is met, one finds God, who takes away all sorrow. ॥16॥
1422.12: The manmukh who does service, with his mind set on the love of another:
(to him) son, wife and family are (all), and he increases attachment to Maya.
In the Lord's court the account is called for; at the end no one can set (him) free.
Without the Name all is sorrow; attachment to Maya brings pain.
O Nanak, (one to whom) through the Guru (the Lord) has come into sight: all attachment to Maya falls away from him. ॥17॥
1423.1: The Gurmukh obeys the Husband's Hukam, and through the Hukam finds peace.
He serves the Hukam, worships the Hukam, and stays merged in the Hukam.
The Hukam is (his) fasting, vow, purity and self-restraint; (by it) he obtains the fruit the mind longs for.
She is ever a happy wife who understands the Hukam and serves the True Guru, lovingly attuned.
O Nanak, those on whom he shows his grace, he unites (with himself) through the Hukam. ॥18॥
1423.2: The poor manmukh (bride) does not understand the Hukam; she ever does her deeds in Haumai.
Fasts, vows, purity, self-restraint and worship: (by such) hypocrisy doubt does not go.
Within, they are impure, pierced through by attachment to Maya, like the elephant that, (after bathing,) throws dust over itself.
They do not remember the One who created (them); without remembering (him), how can one find peace?
O Nanak, the Creator made the world's expanse from the very first; (each) acts out what was written from before. ॥19॥
1423.3: Through the Guru faith has come and the mind is won over; serving night and day, (one) stays merged (in him).
The True Guru, the Guru, is within (him); all worship (him), and all come to behold the True Guru's sight.
One should put faith in the True Guru, supreme in reflection, meeting whom all thirst and hunger go.
I am ever, ever a sacrifice to my Guru, who unites (me) with the True God.
O Nanak, they have received true grace who have come and fallen at the Guru's feet. ॥20॥
1423.4: Those who have love for the Beloved: those friends are with me.
Within and without I roam, yet I keep (the Lord) cherished in the heart. ॥21॥
1423.5: Those who have meditated with one mind and one heart, fixing their minds on the True Guru:
their pain, hunger and the great disease of Haumai are gone; lovingly attuned, they have become free of fault.
They sing (his) virtues, utter (his) virtues, and (each) sleeps merged in (his) virtues.
O Nanak, (they) have found (him) through the perfect Guru; in Sahaj God has come and met (them). ॥22॥
1423.6: The manmukh is attached to Maya; no love for the Naam takes hold (of him).
He practises falsehood, hoards falsehood, and makes falsehood his food.
(The manmukhs) die heaping up the wealth of Maya, which is poison, and in the end it all turns to ashes.
They perform rites and religious duties, ritual purity and self-restraint, (but) within them is greed, (and) vice.
O Nanak, whatever the manmukh does is not accepted; in the Lord's court he is put to shame. ॥23॥
1423.7: Among all the raags that one is good, O brother, by which (the Lord) comes to dwell in the mind.
Such raag and naad (melody and sound) are all true; their worth cannot be told.
(The Lord) is beyond raag and naad; by these his Hukam cannot be understood.
O Nanak, for those who understand the Hukam, (all) comes right; this understanding comes from the True Guru.
Everything has come about from him, as is his will. ॥24॥
1424.1: In the True Guru is the Amrit Name; he utters the Amrit and has (others) utter it.
Through the Guru's teaching (comes) the pure Name: meditate on the pure Name.
The Amrit Bani is the essence; through the Guru it comes to dwell in the mind.
The lotus of the heart blossoms, and the light is merged in the Light.
O Nanak, he has brought the True Guru to those on whose foreheads good fortune was written from the very first. ॥25॥
1424.2: Within is the fire of craving; the manmukh's hunger does not go.
Attachment and family are all false; he stays entangled in the false.
Night and day he broods on his worries; bound by worry he departs.
His birth and death do not end, (as) he does his deeds in Haumai.
In the Guru's refuge he is saved; O Nanak, (the Guru) sets (him) free. ॥26॥
1424.3: The True Guru, the Being, meditates on the Lord; the Sat Sangat (abides) in the True Guru's love.
Those who serve the True Guru in the Sat Sangat, the Lord, through the Guru, unites with himself.
This world and universe is a terrifying ocean; the Guru is the ship that carries (us) across by the Name.
The Guru's Sikhs have accepted (his) will; the perfect Guru carries (them) across.
O Lord, grant (us) the dust of the Guru's Sikhs, that we sinners too may attain salvation.
O Nanak, (the one on whose) forehead the Lord God wrote (it) from the beginning has come and met the Guru.
He (the Guru) has beaten and destroyed Jam's servants, and sets (him) free in the Lord's court.
Acclaim to the Guru's Sikhs: the Lord, well pleased, has united them in union (with himself). ॥27॥
1424.4: The perfect Guru, who has driven out doubt from within, has made the Lord's Name firm (in a person).
Singing the Name of Ram and the Lord's praise, and making it a light, (the Guru) has shown him the way.
Having slain Haumai, he is lovingly attuned to the One, and has enshrined the Naam within.
Through the Guru's teaching Jam cannot even cast an eye on him; he has merged in the True Name.
The Creator himself is at work in all; whoever pleases him, he attaches to the Name.
Servant Nanak lives when he takes the Name; without the Name, in an instant he dies. ॥28॥
1424.5: Within the mind is the disease of Haumai; through Haumai the Saakats, the wicked, are lost in doubt.
O Nanak, meet the True Guru, the Saadh, the friend, and be rid of this disease. ॥29॥
1424.6: (The soul-bride who) through the Guru's teaching utters the Lord's Name, Har Har,
drawn by the Lord's love, is steeped in the Lord day and night, her robe (the body) dyed in the Lord's colour.
No being like the Lord is to be found; I have searched the whole world and seen it.
The Name has been made firm (in me) by the Guru, the True Guru; (my) mind does not waver towards anything else.
Servant Nanak is the Lord's slave, and of the Guru, the True Guru, the slave of slaves. ॥30॥
1425.1: Saloks, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Those who do not turn their faces away, who have come to know the Master: they alone are dyed (in his love).
The unripe lovers, for whom (love) did not take effect, fall away again and again. ॥1॥
1425.2: Without the Master, silks and satins I have burnt in the fire;
says Nanak, rolling in the dust I look beautiful, O Husband, (when I am) with you. ॥2॥
1425.3: Through the Guru's Shabad one should worship (the Lord); through the Naam and love comes detachment.
The five enemies are conquered; O Nanak, (then) this Raag Maru is fruitful. ॥3॥
1425.4: When I have the One, then (I have) a hundred thousand; those like you go begging at so many doors.
(Even) a birth as a Brahmin has passed in vain, (when) the One who made (him) is forgotten. ॥4॥
1425.5: In Sorath one should drink that essence which never turns insipid;
O Nanak, the virtues of the Name of Ram should be sung: (by this comes) spotless glory in the Lord's court. ॥5॥
1425.6: Those whom God himself has protected, no one can kill.
Within (such a one) is the treasure of the Naam; he ever cherishes (the Lord's) virtues.
With the one support of the Inaccessible, he keeps God in mind and body.
The colour of boundless love has taken hold (of him); no one can remove it.
Through the Guru he sings the Lord's virtues and enjoys peace in Sahaj.
O Nanak, he keeps the treasure of the Naam enshrined in his heart, deep within. ॥6॥
1425.7: Whatever (he) does, accept it as good; put away every other reckoning.
(O Lord,) look (on me) with your glance of grace, and attach (me to you) yourself.
Give your servant understanding and teaching, that doubt may go from within.
The writ written from the start: that alone do all act out.
Everything is in his power; there is no other place.
O Nanak, accepting God's will, there is peace and bliss. ॥7॥
1425.8: Those who have remembered the perfect Guru, they alone have been made joyful.
O Nanak, the Name is to be worshipped; (by it life's) purpose is fulfilled. ॥8॥
1425.9: The sinners do (evil) deeds and cry alas, alas;
O Nanak, as the churning-sticks churn (the curd), so Dharam Raj churns (them). ॥9॥
1425.10: Good friends meditate on the Naam and win the priceless human birth;
O Nanak, those who utter such dharma (the Name) have made the world holy. ॥10॥
1425.11: She who takes evil counsel is stuck in a foul place, (where) the mire (seems) sweet;
O Nanak, they alone are saved who have good fortune on their foreheads. ॥11॥
1425.12: Those steeped in (the love of) their Husband sleep in peace;
(those) parted in love from the Master cry out through all eight pahars. ॥12॥
1425.13: Countless sleep for the sake of false Maya;
O Nanak, they are awake who utter the Naam with the tongue. ॥13॥
1425.14: Seeing the mirage and the peopled cities of the gandharvas, (people) go astray;
those who have worshipped the True One, O Nanak, are beautiful in mind and body. ॥14॥
1425.15: The Supreme Lord is the uplifter of the fallen, the all-powerful, infinite Being;
whom he saves, O Nanak, that one remembers the Creator. ॥15॥
1426.1: Leave the other, crooked path, and fix your mind on the One;
in other loves, O Nanak, (the soul-bride) is swept away in the current. ॥16॥
1426.2: In the market of three shops (the three qualities of Maya), the traders do their dealing;
the true dealers are those who have loaded the merchandise of Truth. ॥17॥
1426.3: The foolish (soul-bride) does not know the path of love; she wanders astray.
O Nanak, forgetting the Lord, (people) fall into dark hell. ॥18॥
1426.4: Maya is not forgotten by (his) mind; he begs for money and more money.
That God does not come into (his) mind; O Nanak, it is not in his lot. ॥19॥
1426.5: (The wealth) never runs out at all, as long as he himself is merciful.
The Shabad is inexhaustible, O brother; O Nanak, eat and spend (this) wealth and riches. ॥20॥
1426.6: Were I to find wings on sale, I would take them, (paying) an equal weight (of myself);
I would set them on my own body and, searching, find that Friend. ॥21॥
1426.7: The Friend is the true Emperor, the King over the heads of kings;
sitting near him one is adorned; he is the trust of all. ॥22॥
